transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (Redwood CSM), Maya Rodriguez (Head of Platform - LanternWorks), Tom Blake (NetOps), Aisha Khan (SecOps), Rahul Desai (Cloud Engineer)

Summary (auto): quick discovery focused on private VPC onramp, KMS/HSM constraints, peering vs privatelink, and egress/region gating. Action items assigned, pilot lab proposed.

TOPICS: private endpoints, transit gateway options, KMS/HSM key policies, SOC2/PCI considerations, multi-region constraints, egress throughput and NAT/proxy issues.

Transcript: 
00:00 Sofia Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, uh we got folks from lantern works?
00:06 Maya Rodriguez: yeah hi maya here, thanks, and tom, aisha, rahul all on.
00:10 Sofia Patel: awesome. ethan and i will run through the network and security questions, we want to understand your blockers for private deployment.
00:18 Ethan Wu: hi team. just to set expectations, we'll cover three flows: control plane connectivity, inference dataplane (private endpoints/privatelink), and key management / encryption. then we can discuss region gating and latency.
00:29 Tom Blake: good. our big ask is we cannot route traffic over the public internet for models that touch customer data, so privatelink or VPC peering only. also we have strict egress IP whitelisting.
00:40 Aisha Khan: and from security, keys must be customer-managed, ideally HSM-backed. we have an existing AWS CloudHSM and AWS KMS linked to HSM; we need to know how Redwood integrates.
00:52 Ethan Wu: noted — we support customer KMS integration for Private. there are two common patterns: vault-in-customer-account where we store encryption keys in your KMS and Redwood references them via IAM role, or bring-your-own-key with envelope encryption using a customer CMK. we need to validate KMS policy and cross-account roles.
01:08 Rahul Desai: when you say cross-account roles, do you mean Redwood will assume a role in our account, or we give you a role to assume? we have strict guardrails on STS duration and transitive trust.
01:18 Ethan Wu: typically Redwood’s control plane will assume a minimal role for provisioning private endpoints; for dataplane the runtime acts from Redwood-managed subnets in a peered/transit arrangement. we can also do an agent-less model where the runtime is deployed inside your account (Private on-prem variant) if that helps with trust.
01:31 Maya Rodriguez: curious about transit gateway vs direct peering. our infra team prefers TGW for scale but there's a NAT/bastion architecture we already use. any gotchas?
01:40 Ethan Wu: TGW works well for multi-VPC topologies; our recommendation depends on whether you want shared centralized egress. with TGW you avoid a lot of per-VPC peering complexity. downside is you need to ensure route table limits and blackhole prevention. also privatelink (interface endpoints) are simpler from a security review perspective — traffic never leaves AWS fabric but you still need to manage ENI quotas.
01:58 Tom Blake: ENI quotas are a hard limit for us — we're hitting ENI caps in some test accounts; that could be a blocker for privatelink.
02:05 Ethan Wu: understood. we can model a hybrid: peering/TGW for high-throughput model serving and privatelink for control plane and admin APIs. that reduces ENI surface.
02:15 Aisha Khan: what about IP addressing? we have overlapping CIDRs across our org, so standard peering won't work.
02:22 Ethan Wu: TGW can do route isolation but if CIDRs overlap you may need a NAT/proxy hop or run the runtime in your account (Redwood private managed). another pattern is to use a VPN or private interconnect with NAT translation. we'll draft options.
02:33 Rahul Desai: latency numbers — we expect p50 token latency under 120ms to meet product SLAs. if model inference is in a different region, that won't work. can you pin region?
02:42 Sofia Patel: yes, customers pin model versions to specific region clusters; for Private deployments you can choose which region the runtime is deployed. we have region availability matrix, we'll send.
02:52 Maya Rodriguez: great. related, we have a data residency requirement for EU data that must not leave eu-west-1. is that supported?
02:59 Ethan Wu: absolutely — we deploy private runtime into the customer-chosen region. for Hosted, we have region fallbacks, but Private ensures data never egresses region unless configured.
03:07 Tom Blake: can Redwood's control plane be VPC-peered or is it out of band? our security team prefers no external control plane traffic.
03:14 Sofia Patel: Redwood Private allows options: a private control plane connector over privatelink or a self-hosted control plane where the management plane runs inside your VPC and we communicate over an authenticated channel. both options are documented in the security packet.
03:25 Aisha Khan: about KMS — our compliance requires HSM attested keys, and we need audit logs showing key usage per-request. does Redwood pass key usage logs back into our CloudTrail?
03:36 Ethan Wu: when you own the CMK in your account, all KMS usage is recorded in your CloudTrail. if keys are in your account and Redwood assumes a role, the KMS decryption calls appear under that role's principal — you'll see request logs. if we manage keys we can provide audit exports but customers often prefer customer-managed CMKs for auditability.
03:52 Maya Rodriguez: any constraints with FIPS or gov-cloud-like regions?
03:56 Ethan Wu: support is region-dependent; we have guidance for govcloud and FIPS-enabled endpoints but we need to check model image availability in those regions. we'll include region/distro matrix.
04:05 Tom Blake: egress throughput — some of our workloads need sustained 800 Mbps to the inference endpoints. how does Redwood handle high throughput from a NAT/gateway perspective?
04:15 Ethan Wu: for high throughput we recommend dedicated subnets with large ENI/throughput capacity and avoid per-connection NAT when possible; using TGW and direct peering into Redwood-managed pools or deploying the runtime inside your account avoids NAT throttles. we'll run a capacity plan for your throughput numbers.
04:29 Rahul Desai: on the runtime side, do you support GPU placement in our account? we run on AWS EC2 G5/G5n in some regions; can the Redwood runtime be deployed onto our GPU hosts?
04:38 Ethan Wu: the private on-prem option can run on customer GPUs but requires coordination for drivers and kernel compat. we have an OCI image and an operator; we'll share the operator install doc. for Dedicated we run on our infra — but for Private inside customer VPC we can place on customer hosts with SRE sync.
04:52 Aisha Khan: what about SAML/SSO, RBAC for model access and audit of prompts?
04:58 Sofia Patel: Redwood supports SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is available at org/project/model level. audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via S3 or streaming. we'll include sample mappings.
05:10 Maya Rodriguez: path to pilot — we'd like to run a small POC: private endpoint + KMS CMK in our staging account, run a few requests and validate logs and latency.
05:18 Sofia Patel: perfect. we'd propose a 2-hour hands-on pilot where Ethan walks you through privatelink creation, role setup, and a couple of inference calls. prep: we need IAM role details and a test VPC.
05:28 Tom Blake: note — our company policy requires least privilege and max 1-hour STS tokens, is that supported?
05:34 Ethan Wu: we can work with short STS TTLs, though some automation workflows prefer longer. we'll document the minimal set of permissions and a pattern for short-lived credentials.
05:44 Speaker 1 (Ethan?): there might be some transcription noise here, sorry if names are off.
05:47 Sofia Patel: all good. jumping into a couple of gotchas we often see — ENI quotas for privatelink, overlapping CIDRs, and egress IP preservation for downstream partners who whitelist.
05:57 Rahul Desai: about whitelisting, can you provide static egress IPs from Redwood so partners can allowlist?
06:03 Ethan Wu: yes if you use Dedicated/reserved pools we can route through static NAT egress IPs; for hosted private onramp the pattern is to egress through your TGW/NAT so partner sees your IP. we'll outline both.
06:14 Aisha Khan: encryption at rest — we need assurance tokens and periodic audits. is Redwood SOC2 Type II and do you provide artifact package?
06:21 Sofia Patel: we are SOC2 Type II; we have a compliance pack (PDF + spreadsheet of controls). we'll send that in the security packet.
06:29 Maya Rodriguez: any penalties or risk during rollouts? like model fallback to hosted if capacity spikes? we want no unexpected data plane failovers to public endpoints.
06:38 Ethan Wu: failover policies are configurable — default is to avoid fallback to public-hosted models for private deployments. we can set strict no-fallback for the pilot.
06:46 Tom Blake: can we do network flow logs and VPC flow telemetry to our Splunk?
06:50 Ethan Wu: yes we can forward VPC flow logs and Redwood audit trails to your S3 or streaming endpoint for ingestion into Splunk/Datadog.
06:58 Maya Rodriguez: timeline question — procurement needs a 60-day lead for legal review; we are hoping to start pilot in two weeks. is that realistic?
07:06 Sofia Patel: for pilot we can start within two weeks; legal/procurement for enterprise contract will take longer. we'll provide an NDA + security packet now to expedite their review.
07:13 Rahul Desai: quick follow-up: what ports/protocols need to be open for privatelink and control plane?
07:18 Ethan Wu: control plane typically needs outbound HTTPS to our control endpoint via privatelink (no open public), and dataplane uses gRPC over TLS on configurable ports — we'll include a minimal firewall rules list in the packet.
07:30 Tom Blake: is there a minimum commitment for Private?
07:34 Sofia Patel: pilot has no commitment; for full Private deployment there are two options: reserved capacity or bring-your-own infra. we'll go over pricing after the pilot.
07:42 Aisha Khan: final question: can we do HSM attestation with AWS CloudHSM plus KMS? we need FIPS 140-2 level 3 for some keys.
07:50 Ethan Wu: we generally defer to the customer's KMS for HSM attestation; if you own a FIPS 140-2 HSM-backed KMS and grant Redwood limited decrypt rights (or run runtime in your account) that covers attestation. we'll validate the attestation flow in the security doc.
08:02 Sofia Patel: ok, let's recap next steps and action items. ethan will draw the architecture options (TGW vs privatelink hybrid), i'll send the security packet + SOC2 artifacts, tom will share ENI quota and egress numbers, maya will provide a staging VPC for the pilot.
08:18 Maya Rodriguez: yes i'll share the VPC map and firewall rules by end of week.
08:22 Tom Blake: i'll ping quota team and share ENI limits.
08:24 Aisha Khan: we'll review the KMS IAM policies and send a redacted sample.
08:27 Sofia Patel: perfect. we'll schedule the 2-hour pilot for week of 9/27, looking for a Wednesday or Thursday, we'll follow up in calendar invite.
08:36 Ethan Wu: any other blockers?
08:38 Rahul Desai: none from me, thanks.
08:40 Sofia Patel: thanks everyone for your time. we'll follow up by EOD with the packet and a proposed pilot slot.
